subdomain: 4.2 Design evaluation datasets and test frameworks using mixed methodologies

en.question: An incident assistant returns required categorical fields plus a narrative explaining the likely cause. Field validity has exact rules, while narrative adequacy requires technical judgment. Which evaluation design best fits both contracts?

options.text: Grade the fields and narrative by exact match against one reference response.
options.note: Exact checks suit the categorical fields, but a valid technical explanation can use different wording. One reference string would reject acceptable narrative alternatives.

options.text: Check fields in code and grade narratives with an expert-calibrated rubric.
options.note: Deterministic checks enforce the exact field contract, while a rubric can assess nuanced explanation quality. Calibrating any model grader against expert judgments checks whether its scores reflect the intended criteria.

options.text: Ask a model grader for one overall score covering fields and narrative.
options.note: A single holistic score can overlook an invalid required field and substitutes variable judgment for an available exact check. It also needs calibration before narrative scores can be trusted.

options.text: Have experts review narratives and use narrative scores for the whole response.
options.note: Expert narrative review does not establish that the categorical fields satisfy their exact rules. The field contract should be checked explicitly rather than inferred from prose quality.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
